newsitem.title: PERU: Peru sets Luz del Sur share sale start for Nov 18.
newsitem.headline: Peru sets Luz del Sur share sale start for Nov 18.

text.p: The government will start selling its shares in electricity distributor Luz del Sur on November 18 with an offer of shares to Peruvian nationals, officials said on Wednesday.

"The official date for the start of the Luz del Sur sale is November 18," Jose Carlos Pla, general manager at Banco Continental, the Peruvian bank coordinating the domestic part of the share sale, told Reuters.
Bank officials could not say when the foreign portion of the sale would begin, although an international roadshow to drum up interest will start in Chile on November 21.
Privatization officials expect to set the price for the placement of the state's shares on December 6.
The government holds 30 percent of the utility, but has not specified what proportion it will sell. It hopes to raise $200 million from the privatization.
Officials from investment bank CS First Boston chosen by the government to handle the international portion of the sale -- expect the placement to raise about $100 million abroad.
The domestic portion will be divided into two parts.

In the sale of shares to individual Peruvians under the Citizens' Participation in Privatization plan Banco Continental will direct a group of local banks, including Banco de Credito, Interbanc and Banco Wiese.

In the second part, Spain's Banco Santander has been selected to handle the placement with local institutions. The Spanish bank's brokerage in Peru, Santander SAB, will direct a group of local brokerages to deal with institutions such as local pension funds, insurance companies and banks.

In June 1994, a consortium consisting of Chile's Chilquinta International Inc. and Canada's Ontario Hydro Inc. bought a 60 percent stake in Luz del Sur, a former state-run electricity company for $212.1 million. Another 10 percent is owned by the company's workers.
